summary: This week centered on the UAP Disclosure Forum held in Washington and the legislative push for whistleblower protections. Rep. Luna and other lawmakers are backing immunity measures for a specific list of UAP witnesses, while experts stressed that without legal safeguards from retaliation, potential disclosures could stall. The forum surfaced recurring concerns about military encounters near U.S. bases that have left defense officials unable to explain the incidents, alongside discussions about how religious institutions might help prepare the public for extraterrestrial disclosure. Meanwhile, newly released documents from AARO show the Pentagon and intelligence community have authorized information sharing with the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office, though the Defense Department continues citing national security to withhold core evaluation details. The FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act briefing deadline arrives this week, with expectations that Congress will once again press for concrete UAP findings.
